=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines ~419-427 (the "Prepare template-only PR live copies for parity tests" step, `run:` block)
  PROBLEM: When the initial `before` is empty / all-zeros / unreachable AND `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` also fails, the warning message printed before reassignment says `using merge-base with main (unavailable)`, but the script is then invoked with `--before ""` (the empty `${fallback}`). The "using merge-base with main" prefix reads as if the fallback was successfully applied even though no SHA was found and `before` was reset to empty.
  WHY IT FAILS AT RUNTIME: Operator-facing log message contradicts the actual invocation; someone reviewing the warning will think parity drift recovery was attempted, when it was not. This is a documentation discrepancy rather than a runtime crash because `sync_claude_live_copies.py` is documented to skip drift recovery on empty `--before` — but the warning text is misleading.
  severity=NIT | confidence=3
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines ~419-427 (the "Prepare template-only PR live copies for parity tests" step, `run:` block, in conjunction with `agents.d/7121-ci-orchestrator-integration-branches.md`)
  PROBLEM: When the initial `before` is invalid AND `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` also returns empty, the step falls through to `python3 scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py sync --dry-run --before "" --after HEAD ...`. The fragment and inline comment claim "the step uses the merge-base of `HEAD` with `origin/main`", but in the all-fail case nothing is used. The PR description's testing section explicitly enumerates empty / all-zero / unreachable / valid `before` values and asserts only that "the valid one is kept" — it does not pin behaviour or message wording for the case where merge-base itself fails.
  WHY IT FAILS AT RUNTIME: The implementation handles the failure silently with a misleading message; it does not crash. The risk is operator confusion, not data corruption.
  severity=NIT | confidence=3
- agents.d/7121-ci-orchestrator-integration-branches.md: line 1 (the `<!-- agents: section="..." -->` marker)
  PROBLEM: The fragment's marker targets `Interactive slash-command model selection`, a section that (per its body) covers `.claude/commands/*.md` model pins, `/implement-plan-claude` and `/implement-issue-claude` hand-offs, and Live `.claude/` copy sync. The fragment's content is about CI trigger patterns, the parity-preparation step's `before` fallback, the workflow-failure heal intake, and `budget-watch`. None of those topics belong under the slash-command-model-selection heading; they belong in the `Workflow architecture` section (which already enumerates every pipeline phase including `ci.yml` checks) or in a new dedicated CI-triggers block.
  WHY IT FAILS AT RUNTIME: Assembled `agents.md` readers looking for CI trigger / parity prep behaviour will not find it under `Workflow architecture`, and the `Interactive slash-command model selection` section's contract as a model-selection reference is degraded by hosting topic-mismatched paragraphs. No runtime failure.

  WHY IT FAILS AT RUNTIME: The step still exits 0 and downstream parity tests report drift as designed (fail-closed on drift), so there is no functional break, but the operator-facing warning misstates what happened: no merge-base was used and no preparation ran.
